output.brief: The jump in chilled write-offs is mostly a dock problem, not a Haverlow or refrigeration problem. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four on 27 July, pallets wait about 3 hours 50 minutes between unloading and reaching a chamber, up from 44 minutes. They sit in unrefrigerated staging at 15–17°C. Night write-offs rose to about 3% across all suppliers, including Pellridge and own-label, while day shift barely moved. Haverlow's trailers arrived at 2.4–3.5°C on independent telemetry, and the chambers held 2–4°C, so a Haverlow chargeback and volume move would punish the wrong party. Confidence is moderate-to-good. The main gaps are that no claim-level data tests the Corriebank credit rise, and the arrival-temperature finding rests on load-level pairs for four loads. Next: restore the night team to six, set a maximum dock-to-chamber time monitored weekly, and reconcile a sample of Corriebank claims. Hold the Haverlow chargeback and do not remove the receiving probe.
